cigarettes.title: Doll et al. (BMJ): 50-year study on smoking and mortality
cigarettes.authors: Doll R, Peto R, Boreham J, Sutherland I
cigarettes.keyFindings: Heavy smoking (20+ cigarettes/day) reduces life expectancy by 10-13 years on average. Quitting at any age provides substantial health benefits.

cigarettes.title: Hackshaw et al. (BMJ): Light smoking and cardiovascular disease
cigarettes.authors: Hackshaw A, Morris JK, Boniface S, Tang JL, Milenković D
cigarettes.keyFindings: Even light smoking (1-5 cigarettes/day) increases cardiovascular disease risk by 50-60% compared to non-smokers. No safe level of smoking exists.

water.title: Popkin et al. (Nutrition Reviews): Hydration and health
water.authors: Popkin BM, D'Anci KE, Rosenberg IH
water.keyFindings: Adequate hydration (8+ glasses/day) is essential for cognitive function, physical performance, and reducing kidney stone risk. Chronic dehydration increases health complications.

water.title: IOM (National Academies): Dietary reference intakes for water
water.keyFindings: Recommended daily water intake: 3.7L for men, 2.7L for women (including all beverages and food). Individual needs vary by activity level, climate, and health status.

alcohol.title: Wood et al. (Lancet): Alcohol and cardiovascular mortality
alcohol.authors: Wood AM, Kaptoge S, Butterworth AS, et al.
alcohol.keyFindings: Heavy drinking (4+ drinks/day) reduces life expectancy by 5-10 years. Even moderate drinking increases cardiovascular and cancer risks.

alcohol.title: GBD 2016 Alcohol Collaborators (Lancet): Global alcohol burden
alcohol.keyFindings: The safest level of alcohol consumption is none. Even low levels of drinking increase health risks, particularly for cancer and injuries.

walking.title: Lee et al. (JAMA): Steps per day and all-cause mortality
walking.authors: Lee IM, Shiroma EJ, Kamada M, Bassett DR, Matthews CE, Buring JE
walking.keyFindings: Taking 7,000-10,000 steps/day significantly reduces all-cause mortality. Even 4,000 steps/day shows benefits compared to sedentary lifestyle.

walking.title: Paluch et al. (Lancet Public Health): Steps and longevity
walking.authors: Paluch AE, Bajpai S, Bassett DR, et al.
walking.keyFindings: For adults 60+, 6,000-8,000 steps/day is optimal for reducing mortality risk. For younger adults, 8,000-10,000 steps provides maximum benefit.

sleep.title: Cappuccio et al. (Sleep): Sleep duration and all-cause mortality
sleep.authors: Cappuccio FP, D'Elia L, Strazzullo P, Miller MA
sleep.keyFindings: Both short (<6 hours) and long (>9 hours) sleep duration are associated with increased mortality risk. Optimal sleep is 7-8 hours per night.

sleep.title: Watson et al. (Sleep Health): Recommended sleep duration
sleep.authors: Watson NF, Badr MS, Belenky G, et al.
sleep.keyFindings: National Sleep Foundation recommends 7-9 hours for adults 18-64, and 7-8 hours for adults 65+. Quality matters as much as quantity.

heart_rate.title: Fox et al. (Lancet): Resting heart rate and cardiovascular outcomes
heart_rate.authors: Fox K, Borer JS, Camm AJ, et al.
heart_rate.keyFindings: Elevated resting heart rate (>80 bpm) is associated with increased cardiovascular mortality. Each 10 bpm increase raises risk by 16%.

heart_rate.title: Zhang et al. (CMAJ): Heart rate and longevity
heart_rate.authors: Zhang D, Shen X, Qi X
heart_rate.keyFindings: Resting heart rate >75 bpm doubles cardiovascular disease risk. Regular exercise can reduce resting heart rate by 10-15 bpm.

general.title: Khaw et al. (PLoS Medicine): Combined lifestyle factors and mortality
general.authors: Khaw KT, Wareham N, Bingham S, Welch A, Luben R, Day N
general.keyFindings: Four healthy behaviors (not smoking, being active, moderate drinking, eating 5 fruits/vegetables daily) can add 14 years to life expectancy.

general.title: Li et al. (Circulation): Healthy lifestyle and life expectancy
general.authors: Li Y, Pan A, Wang DD, et al.
general.keyFindings: Five low-risk lifestyle factors (healthy diet, regular exercise, healthy weight, moderate alcohol, no smoking) at age 50 project 14 years longer life for women and 12 years for men.

general.title: Akesson et al. (Archives of Internal Medicine): Low-risk lifestyle and mortality
general.authors: Akesson A, Larsson SC, Discacciati A, Wolk A
general.keyFindings: Men with 5 low-risk factors (healthy diet, normal weight, moderate alcohol, no smoking, physically active) had 86% lower cardiovascular mortality risk.

general.title: Ford et al. (Circulation): Healthy lifestyle and chronic disease
general.authors: Ford ES, Bergmann MM, Kröger J, Schienkiewitz A, Weikert C, Boeing H
general.keyFindings: Four healthy lifestyle factors reduce risk of major chronic diseases by 78%: never smoking, BMI <30, 3.5+ hours exercise/week, healthy diet score.

elderly_specific.title: Rizzuto et al. (BMJ): Lifestyle and mortality in the elderly
elderly_specific.authors: Rizzuto D, Orsini N, Qiu C, Wang HX, Fratiglioni L
elderly_specific.keyFindings: For people 75+, maintaining 4-5 healthy lifestyle factors (rich social network, moderate alcohol, no smoking, leisure activities, physical activity) can extend survival by 5 years.

elderly_specific.title: Sabia et al. (BMJ): Healthy behaviors and compression of morbidity
elderly_specific.authors: Sabia S, Singh-Manoux A, Hagger-Johnson G, et al.
elderly_specific.keyFindings: Adopting healthy behaviors in middle age delays onset of disability by 5-6 years, compressing morbidity into shorter period at end of life.
